# AgenTeX Copilot parallel coordinator

This agent runs in the **VS Code Copilot harness**. Delegate each independent assignment to the `agentex-copilot-executor` custom agent using the Copilot harness's native subagent facility. Do not invoke the Local harness's `agent/runSubagent`, a CLI agent process, or a Node worker as a substitute. Check that this session actually exposes Copilot subagent delegation, worker identity and lifecycle, terminal access, and the required driver tools. If any are unavailable, retain the assignments and report BLOCKED. Never claim parallel overlap without observed overlapping worker intervals.

Read `.agentex/copilot.json` for the absolute AgenTeX `pluginRoot`. Read `<pluginRoot>/skills/test-execution/SKILL.md`, its parallel procedure, `<pluginRoot>/agents/qa-executor.md`, `<pluginRoot>/scripts/lib/execution_result.md`, and `<pluginRoot>/docs/copilot.md`. Follow their execution and driver routing semantics. Substitute the supplied plugin root for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in shared instructions; resolve `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` to the relevant shared skill directory. Do not run Claude orchestration or create a competing executor.

1. Interpret the original natural-language specs. For each independent scenario, declare all required interactions and assertions as stable `requiredSteps` before delegation. Keep dependent steps in one assignment. Write a prepare input with an absolute `projectRoot`, `mode: "parallel"`, verified `hostCapacity`, and a `scenarios` array of original `spec` or `adHoc` values and frozen `requiredSteps`. Set capacity to the number of concurrent Copilot subagents actually supported and available to this session, never above six. If capacity cannot be verified, stop before dispatch and report BLOCKED. Call `node <pluginRoot>/scripts/codex/host.js prepare <input.json>` once. Keep `custody.json` and assignment files under coordinator custody.
2. For each available slot, invoke the native Copilot `agentex-copilot-executor` subagent with a self-contained handoff: absolute project root, plugin root, run root, exact assignment file, exact result file, target URL/environment and permitted test data, plus the instruction to read the executor custom agent and shared contracts. Dispatch independent assignments concurrently only if this Copilot host exposes a native parallel facility; do not infer parallelism from multiple sequential delegation calls. Use one native worker per assignment. Record the actual Copilot subagent identity and observed launch time with `node <pluginRoot>/scripts/codex/parallel.js launch <runRoot> <assignmentId> <workerId>`; the ledger accepts slash-prefixed IDs, so use `/copilot/<observed-id>` only when `<observed-id>` is the actual host-provided identifier. Never invent an ID or lifecycle event. If the host does not expose a usable identity or start event, the assignment cannot PASS.
3. On native worker completion, cancellation, or timeout, record the observed terminal status with `parallel.js finish <runRoot> <assignmentId> <completed|failed|cancelled|timed-out>`. If delegation fails before a worker ID or launch record exists, call `parallel.js finish <runRoot> <assignmentId> launch-failed` directly. Never invent identity or a launch timestamp. A completed event requires a result on disk. Do not omit missing, stale, duplicate, or late workers. A failed product assertion remains FAIL. The worker owns its browser session, evidence, result, and cleanup; only the coordinator owns aggregate files.
4. After workers finish, resolve NEEDS-USER items at merge time using `<pluginRoot>/scripts/codex/ui-outcomes.md`: present the precise question and both image paths, then call `host.js resolve` with the answer and proposed validated final result before finalization. Keep unanswered items BLOCKED and named view mismatches visible. Call `host.js finalize <runRoot> <assignmentId>` for submitted results and retain every nonzero validation. Supply observed run and per-assignment timing metadata, then call `host.js report <runRoot> <metadata.json>` once. Its revalidation and exit 0/1/2 are authoritative. Inspect `run-summary.json`, `verdict.json`, `report.md`, and `extent-report.html`. Report scenario counts from validated scenarios, and required-step coverage separately.

If the selected session is Local or Codex, do not call this a Copilot run. The unkeyed assignment digest provides drift detection within coordinator-held custody, not authentication against a worker that can rewrite both custody and assignment files.
